reasons.text: Buys feedstock inside a closed loop of 3 recyclers trading the same material (70% of its feedstock)
Claimed tonnage in the busiest month would need 213% of the plant's connected load running non-stop (above 100% is physically impossible)
Certificates claim more than the declared monthly capacity in 60% of months
Category III share of certificates is 68%, +66% versus what its process route can produce
Sold products equal only 20% of the output expected from the tonnes claimed
100% of certificate tonnes were sold below the cost of recycling (average 0.17x the cost floor)

inspection_checklist: Trace the material flow between the plants in the loop (weighbridge slips, vehicle GPS); the same tonnes may be invoiced round a ring.
Obtain the DISCOM consumption statement and meter readings for the flagged months; compare connected machinery (kW) against the claimed tonnage.
Check installed machinery and shift records against the declared capacity; request production registers for the flagged months.
Cross-check the certificate generation dates and category mix against the plant's process route and stock registers.
Reconcile product sales with processed tonnes; contact the product buyers listed and verify that they received the material.
Ask for the plant's cost sheet; certificates priced below the cost of recycling imply the processing cost was never incurred.
